title: Iran's provinces · The south and the east · GeoClick Geography
edition: Regions of Europe · one lesson per country · November 2026
intro: Welcome to Iran's provinces, part 2 of 2. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
We work through 15 of the Iran regions the map names, once each: where it sits, one fact worth keeping, and a hook to remember it by.

states.name: Razavi Khorasan
lines: Razavi Khorasan fills the north-east of Iran around Mashhad, its largest city, on the road east towards Afghanistan and Turkmenistan.
The name Razavi is for Imam Reza, the eighth imam of Shia Islam, whose shrine is at Mashhad, and most of the world’s saffron is grown in this province.
Remember the eastern province with the great shrine at Mashhad, the tomb of the poet Ferdowsi at Tus and the saffron fields around it.
states.transition: Let's bring Razavi Khorasan into view.

states.name: Kermanshah
lines: Kermanshah lies in the west of Iran at the foot of the Zagros, with the city of Kermanshah as its largest city, south of Kurdistan and north of Ilam.

The province was called Bakhtaran after the revolution until its historical name was restored in the early 1990s, and at Bisotun Darius recorded his victories in three languages, which helped scholars read cuneiform.
Remember the province whose name was changed and changed back, with the cliff inscription that unlocked the cuneiform script.

states.name: Lorestan
lines: Lorestan runs through the western mountains, the Zagros country north of Khuzestan, with Khorramabad as its largest city, standing in a bend of the river.
Its name means land of the Lurs, and the Luristan bronzes, decorated weapons and horse fittings of the Iron Age, come from this region and from neighbouring Ilam.
Remember the land of the Lurs, where the bronze axes and horse fittings of the Iron Age were found in the Zagros valleys.

states.name: Ilam
lines: Ilam is the small south-western province where the Zagros meets the low plains of Khuzestan, with the city of Ilam in its north, high above the marshes.
The territory was known as Poshtkuh-e Lorestan before the name Ilam was adopted, and the mound of Ali Kosh near Dehloran preserves evidence of Neolithic settlement.
Remember the little south-western province, where the Neolithic mounds of Ali Kosh show how early people lived off the land.

states.name: Isfahan
lines: Isfahan lies in the centre of Iran, the green valley of the Zayanderud river between the Zagros and the desert, with the city of Isfahan in the middle of it.
The name appears as Spahan in Sasanian inscriptions describing the province, the houses of Abyaneh are coated in red earth, and Kashan still grows roses for its rose water.
Remember the green river valley in the middle of the country, the red-earth village of Abyaneh and the roses of Kashan.

states.name: Yazd
lines: Yazd stands in the centre-east of Iran, on the edge of the desert where the mountains give way to sand, with the city of Yazd at its heart.

Its name is possibly connected with the Sasanian king Yazdegerd I, the Zoroastrian shrine of Chak Chak near Ardakan attracts a pilgrimage every June, and Meybod still weaves zilu floor coverings from cotton yarn.
Remember the desert city that kept its old wind towers, the fire temple above it and the woven floor rugs of Meybod.

states.name: South Khorasan
lines: South Khorasan lies in the east of Iran, with Birjand as its largest city, between the old Khorasan in the north and the Baluch lands in the south.
It was created in 2004 from Khorasan, a name referring to the rising sun or the east, and the Akbariyeh garden at Birjand is one of the nine Persian gardens inscribed by UNESCO.
Remember the eastern province cut off in 2004, with a UNESCO garden at Birjand and the saffron fields of Qaen nearby.
states.transition: Let's bring South Khorasan into view.

states.name: Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari
lines: Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari is a high province in the centre-west, on the Zagros plateau above Khuzestan, with Shahrekord as its largest city and Isfahan on its eastern edge.
Chaharmahal means four regions and Bakhtiari names the tribal community, whose herders still move their flocks between summer grazing grounds around Shahrekord and winter quarters down in Khuzestan.
Remember the four regions of the Bakhtiari, whose herders walk their flocks down to the warm lowlands each winter.
states.transition: Let's bring Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari into view.

states.name: Khuzestan
lines: Khuzestan is the south-western province at the head of the Persian Gulf, low and flat, with Ahvaz as its largest city where the Karun and Dez rivers run.
The name probably means the land of the Khuz, an old name for the people of Susa, and at Chogha Zanbil stands one of the few ziggurats left outside Mesopotamia.
Remember the low green province at the head of the Gulf, where the stepped tower of Chogha Zanbil still stands.

states.name: Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad
lines: Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad lies in the south-west, above the Persian Gulf coast, with Yasuj as its largest city high among the folds of the Zagros.

The name joins the old region of Kohgiluyeh with the Boyer-Ahmadi tribal group, who speak a Luri language of the south-western Iranian group, and near Shush two limestone pillars called Dogur Dopa still puzzle visitors.
Remember the two strange pillars above Shush, and the tribe that gives the province its second name.
states.transition: Let's bring Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad into view.

states.name: Fars
lines: Fars lies in the south-central part of Iran, the land the Persians came from, with Shiraz as its largest city and the Zagros rising along its western edge.

Pars, the old name of this land, gave its name to Persia and to Farsi, and at Persepolis the ceremonial capital of Darius was burned by Alexander in 330 BC, while the tomb of Cyrus the Great stands at Pasargadae.
Remember the homeland of the Persians, where Alexander burned Persepolis and Cyrus is buried at Pasargadae.

states.name: Kerman
lines: Kerman lies in the south-east of Iran, a dry province of high plains and desert between Fars in the west and the coast of Hormozgan in the south, with the city of Kerman in its north.

The mud-brick citadel of Bam was largely destroyed in the earthquake of 2003, which killed about 26,000 people, and satellites have measured the hottest ground temperatures on Earth in the Lut desert to the east.
Remember the hot desert province, where the ground has been measured hotter than anywhere else on Earth and the citadel of Bam fell in 2003.

states.name: Bushehr
lines: Bushehr runs along the Persian Gulf coast in the south-west, a narrow green strip between the mountains and the water, with the city of Bushehr on the shore.
The island port of Siraf was one of the great ports of the Gulf around the tenth century, trading as far as China, and Iran’s first nuclear power station, near Bushehr, began supplying power in 2011.
Remember the narrow Gulf coast, where the old island port of Siraf traded with China.

states.name: Sistan and Baluchestan
lines: Sistan and Baluchestan is the great south-eastern province, stretching from the Afghan border to the shore of the Gulf of Oman, with Zahedan as its largest city in the north.

Sistan comes from Sakastan, the land of the Saka, and Baluchestan is named for the Baluch people, and at Shahr-i Sokhta archaeologists found a prosthetic eye in a grave dated to about 2900 to 2800 BC.
Remember the far south-east, where the oldest known artificial eye was dug out of the mound of Shahr-i Sokhta.
states.transition: Let's bring Sistan and Baluchestan into view.

states.name: Hormozgan
lines: Hormozgan wraps around the Strait of Hormuz in the far south, facing the Gulf of Oman and the head of the Persian Gulf, with Bandar Abbas as its largest city on the water.

The province is named for the island and the strait, the Portuguese holding the island from 1507 until Shah Abbas took it with English help in 1622, and about a fifth of the world’s oil passes through the strait.
Remember the strait at the mouth of the Gulf, where a fifth of the world’s oil passes and the Portuguese lost the island to the English.

recap: 15 regions of Iran, one for each target of the map: Razavi Khorasan, Kermanshah, Lorestan, Ilam, Isfahan, Yazd, South Khorasan, Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari, Khuzestan, Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad, Fars, Kerman, Bushehr, Sistan and Baluchestan and Hormozgan.
Remember the shape of Iran from the inside: the regions nest around each other, and every name on the map belongs somewhere in this one country.
